intent_en: To demonstrate that the birth rate in Sub-Saharan Africa remains significantly higher than in other global regions.
previous_intent: To demonstrate that Sub-Saharan Africa's birth rate remains significantly higher than in East Asia, North America, and the European Union, highlighting a persistent demographic disparity despite slowing growth.
narration_support: Although its growth rate has slowed down in the last few decades, it's still much higher than in the rest of the world.
chart_support: Icon bar chart titled 'Births Per Woman in 2017' showing Sub-Saharan Africa has a much higher value than East Asia, North America, and the European Union.
evidence_note: The narration mentions a high rate compared to the rest of the world despite a slowdown, while the chart visualizes 'Births Per Woman in 2017' with Sub-Saharan Africa (4.7) being much higher than East Asia (1.8), North America (1.7), and the EU (1.6). Note: The narration refers to 'growth rate' while the chart shows 'births per woman' (fertility rate), which are closely related demographic indicators.
